set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c): for PBV development (new construction or rehabilitation under an Agreement to enter into a HAP contract) involving nine or more contract units, owners and contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and the PHA must monitor compliance (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153). Does not apply to PBVs placed on existing housing or developments under nine contract units; state prevailing wage may also apply through HACM as a local public housing authority under Labor Code 1720(c)(1) when HACM or its Development Corporation is a development party.

reason: Federal PBV rule 24 CFR 983.153(c) requires Davis-Bacon wages on PBV development with nine or more contract units.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Director's decision on appeal PW 2006-020(A), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe and PW 2006-005 Central Village Apartments, holds that conduit tax-exempt bond financing (publicly offered or privately placed, including CSCDA issues) is not a payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b) because proceeds and repayments never enter public coffers (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf). A County TEFRA approval adds no public funds. Other sources in the stack (below-market public loans, land, fee waivers, PBVs, HOME or CDBG) can still trigger state or federal prevailing wage on their own terms.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage set false for the conduit bond and TEFRA approval only, per DIR coverage rulings; recheck project stack for other triggers.

reason: DIR coverage ruling PW 2006-020(A) holds conduit bond financing is not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b).

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees that are reduced, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, but 1720(c)(3) excludes de minimis subsidies (under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost) and 1720 does not address fee deferrals; the outcome depends on the size of the waiver and other project funding. Marina Code Chapter 17.48 (zoneomics mirror) contains no prevailing wage provision.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public-funds definition, with outcome depending on 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and project facts.

reason: Searched Labor Code 1720 and Marina Code Chapter 17.48 and found no rule specific to AHO fee waivers or deferrals, so coverage depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis and project facts.
